title: Shopping & money
goal: Ask prices, point out 'this one' and 'that one', bargain politely and buy clothes and groceries.
intro: Money is counted in **ଟଙ୍କା** (rupees). In markets you will need demonstratives — **ଏଇଟା** 'this one', **ସେଇଟା** 'that one' — and some bargaining phrases. Fixed-price shops (malls, handloom emporiums) don't bargain; street markets usually do.

phrases.en: Is there anything a bit cheaper?
Do you have it in another colour?
Please show me a bigger size.

grammar.title: This and that: ଏ / ସେ, ଏଇଟା / ସେଇଟା
grammar.body:
Odia demonstratives are built on **ଏ-** (near: this) and **ସେ-** (far: that):

Before a noun: **ଏହି / ଏଇ / ଏ** 'this', **ସେହି / ସେଇ / ସେ** 'that' — ଏହି ଜାମା 'this shirt'.
Standing alone (things): **ଏଇଟା** (polite ଏହିଟି) 'this one', **ସେଇଟା** (ସେହିଟି) 'that one'; plural **ଏଗୁଡ଼ିକ** 'these', **ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକ** 'those'.
People: **ଏ** 'this person', **ସେ** 'that person', **ଏମାନେ / ସେମାନେ** 'these/those people'.
Asking: **କେଉଁ** 'which', **କେଉଁଟା** 'which one'.

The same pairs run through the language: ଏଠି/ସେଠି 'here/there', ଏବେ/ସେବେ 'now/then', ଏତେ/ସେତେ 'this much/that much', ଏମିତି/ସେମିତି 'like this/like that'.

grammar.title: Prices and bargaining
grammar.body:
Ask **… କେତେ?** ('… how much?') or **…ର ଦାମ କେତେ?** ('what is the price of …?'). Rates per unit use **-କୁ**: କିଲୋକୁ ତିରିଶି ଟଙ୍କା 'thirty rupees a kilo', ଜୋଡ଼ାକୁ 'per pair'.

Bargaining is good-humoured: ଟିକେ କମ କରନ୍ତୁ 'bring it down a bit', ଶେଷ ଦାମ କେତେ? 'what's your final price?', … ଦେବି 'I'll give …'. Saying you'll go to another shop (ଅନ୍ୟ ଦୋକାନରେ ଦେଖିବି) often does the trick.

examples.en: How much are potatoes per kilo?
Please lower the price a bit.

dialogue.title: At the vegetable market
dialogue.setting: Sam buys vegetables from a stall in Unit-1 Market, Bhubaneswar.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Uncle, how much are tomatoes a kilo?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଚାଳିଶି? ବହୁତ ଦାମୀ! ପାଖ ଦୋକାନରେ ତିରିଶି।
lines.roman: chaḷisi? bôhutô dami! pakhô dokanôre tirisi.
lines.en: Forty? Very expensive! At the next stall it's thirty.

lines.speaker: Vendor
lines.en: Look, my tomatoes are absolutely fresh.

lines.speaker: Vendor
lines.en: Okay. How much shall I give you?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଦୁଇ କିଲୋ ଟମାଟୋ ଆଉ ଏକ କିଲୋ ଆଳୁ।
lines.roman: dui kilo ṭômaṭo au ekô kilo aḷu.
lines.en: Two kilos of tomatoes and a kilo of potatoes.

lines.speaker: Vendor
lines.native: ଆଳୁ କିଲୋକୁ କୋଡ଼ିଏ। ସବୁ ମିଶି ନବେ ଟଙ୍କା।
lines.roman: aḷu kiloku koṛie. sôbu misi nôbe ṭôṅka.
lines.en: Potatoes are twenty a kilo. Ninety rupees altogether.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Here you are, a hundred rupees.

culture: Odisha's markets — from Bhubaneswar's Unit-1 *haṭô* to weekly village *haṭs* — are lively places for bargaining, but keep it friendly. UPI phone payments are accepted almost everywhere, even at small stalls. For crafts, try state emporiums like *Utkalika* (fixed prices): Pipili appliqué, Pattachitra paintings, silver filigree and handloom sarees.

tip.title: This and that: ଏହି / ସେହି, ଏଇଟା / ସେଇଟା
tip.body:
- Before a noun: **ଏହି** 'this', **ସେହି** 'that' — ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଗ, ସେହି ଜାମା.
- On their own: **ଏଇଟା** 'this one', **ସେଇଟା** 'that one'.
- Asking: **କେଉଁ** 'which' before a noun, **କେଉଁଟା** 'which one' on its own.
- Before a noun always ଏହି: say ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଗ, not ଏଇଟା ବ୍ୟାଗ.

sentences.en: This bag is nice.
I'll take that one, not this one.
How much is that blue shirt?
Which bag is yours?
This isn't my shirt.
Which one shall I take, this one or that one?
Give me this red bag, please.
You get good shirts in that shop.

sentences.native: ମୋ ଜାମା ପୁରୁଣା, ନୂଆ ଜାମା ଦରକାର।
sentences.roman: mo jama puruṇa, nua jama dôrôkarô.
sentences.en: My shirt is old — I need a new one.

tip.title: Asking the price
tip.body:
- **… କେତେ?** 'how much is …?' — ଏଇଟା କେତେ?
- Or with **-ର** 'of': ଜାମା**ର** ଦାମ କେତେ? 'what's the price of the shirt?'
- Per kilo, per piece: **-କୁ** — କିଲୋ**କୁ** ତିରିଶି ଟଙ୍କା 'thirty rupees a kilo'.
tip.pattern: thing + ର ଦାମ କେତେ?  ·  କିଲୋକୁ + price

sentences.en: How much is this bag?
Potatoes are twenty-five rupees a kilo.
How much is the shirt?
How much are mangoes a kilo?
How much is that one?
Fish is three hundred rupees a kilo.
Two kilos of potatoes, please.
This one's expensive, that one's cheap.
That's really cheap!

tip.title: Bringing the price down
tip.body:
- **ଟିକେ କମ କରନ୍ତୁ** 'bring it down a bit' — said with a smile.
- Make an offer with the future **ଦେବି** 'I'll give': ଦୁଇ ଶହ ଦେବି.
- **ମୁଁ କେବଳ ଦେଖୁଛି** 'I'm just looking'; **ଅନ୍ୟ ଦୋକାନରେ ଦେଖିବି** 'I'll look in another shop' often does the trick.

sentences.en: Brother, bring the price down a bit.
I'll give two hundred rupees.
No, I'll look in another shop.
Is there a discount?
The shopkeeper isn't giving a discount.
We're just looking.

sentences.native: ମୋ ପାଖରେ କେବଳ ପାଞ୍ଚ ଶହ ଟଙ୍କା ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: mo pakhôre kebôḷô pañchô sôhô ṭôṅka ôchhi.
sentences.en: I only have five hundred rupees on me.
Tell me your final price.
It's cheaper in the other shop.

tip.title: Show me…: ଦେଖାନ୍ତୁ
tip.body:
- **ଦେଖାଇବା** 'to show' → polite **ଦେଖାନ୍ତୁ** 'please show'. Don't confuse it with **ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ** 'look'.
- Who to: **ମୋତେ** ଦେଖାନ୍ତୁ 'show me'.
- **ପିନ୍ଧି ଦେଖିବା** 'to try on' (lit. 'wear and see').

sentences.en: Please show me that saree.
Show me some black shoes, please.
These trousers are too small.
Do you have a small size?

sentences.native: ଏହି ଶାଢ଼ୀ ନାଲି ରଙ୍ଗରେ ଅଛି କି?
sentences.roman: ehi saṛhi nali rôṅgôre ôchhi ki?
sentences.en: Do you have this saree in red?
Try this one on. (shopkeeper)
I'm buying new clothes.
Where can I buy shoes?
Is the size right?
No, it's a bit big.
I'll pay in cash.

sentences.native: ପାଞ୍ଚ ଶହ ଟଙ୍କାର ଖୁଚୁରା ଅଛି କି?
sentences.roman: pañchô sôhô ṭôṅkarô khuchura ôchhi ki?

I don't have cash — I'll pay by UPI.
I don't have any money on me.
Please give me change.

sentences.native: ଜାମା ଆଉ ପ୍ୟାଣ୍ଟ ସବୁ ମିଶି କେତେ?
sentences.roman: jama au pyaṇṭ sôbu misi kete?
sentences.en: How much for the shirt and trousers altogether?
I don't need a bag, thanks.
